prompt: Review host hardening for a Linux service fleet built from a mutable VM image. Hosts expose SSH and an internal admin port broadly, several unused daemons/packages remain installed, the service runs under a shared privileged account, patches are applied manually without a rollback policy, and local privilege elevation is poorly audited. Design a secure baseline covering supported image/package lifecycle, dedicated non-root service identity, minimized installed/listening surface, restricted management network path, sudo/admin separation, file/config permissions, logging of privileged/config changes, immutable-image rebuild preference, emergency access, and evidence comparing desired configuration with the running host. Keep cloud-account IAM and resource policies in cloud-security.

requirements: Linux host inventory and package/listener snapshot

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Unused services/packages/listeners are identified and removed/disabled, with the remaining service and management ports tied to explicit operational need.
The application runs under a dedicated non-root identity and administrative privilege is separated, time/audit constrained, and not shared with normal service execution.
SSH/admin interfaces are reachable only from the intended management path and are not exposed on the general service network.
The design defines supported base-image/package update ownership, risk-based remediation timing, rebuild/rollback behavior, and how emergency fixes converge back to managed configuration.
A post-deploy check compares intended packages, listeners, identities, permissions, network exposure, patch versions, and audit controls to actual running state.
